hook: Spinning dust clouds obey the hoop conjecture within 14% if rotational energy counts toward mass
hook_turn: if rotational energy counts toward mass

readout.label: Max hoop coefficient deviation from unity

summary: The hoop conjecture says a black hole forms when enough mass fits inside a small enough hoop in every direction. The authors built initial data for rotating dust shaped like pancakes and baguettes and tested it numerically. It holds when the mass includes rotational energy, but using the ADM mass gives apparent violations up to about 25%. The test covers axisymmetric dust only.
title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
